# Diagnostics and figures

```{r diagnostics}
## =============================================================================
## tail_index_diagnostics_C0331.R
##
## Adapted from tail_index_diagnostics.R. The same diagnostics are applied to
## the OBSERVED clone sizes of PDX C0331-231 instead of synthetic data, and the
## plots are saved as PDF figures for Chapter 4 of the thesis:
##
##   ch4_pareto_tail.pdf   -> Section 4.3.2 (empirical Pareto-tail plots)
##   ch4_hill_plot.pdf     -> Section 4.4   (Hill re-examination)
##   ch4_obrien.pdf        -> Section 4.4   (O'Brien maximum-to-sum diagnostic)
##   ch4_running_mean.pdf  -> Section 4.5   (running means)
##
## The settings follow the main analysis (16.Rmd): controls excluded, dAMSE from
## the R package tea, O'Brien with 40 permutations and 60 sample sizes from 50
## to n, slope cutoff -0.1, seed = 1244 + sgRNA index.
##
## HOW TO RUN: put this script in the same folder as C0331-231.csv and
## signaling1_guides.csv (the folder of 16.Rmd), then source it in RStudio.
## =============================================================================

library(tea)   # dAMSE threshold selection, as in the main analysis

## -----------------------------------------------------------------------
## 0. SETTINGS
## -----------------------------------------------------------------------
data_file      <- "C0331-231.csv"          # positive clone counts
map_file       <- "signaling1_guides.csv"  # sgRNA index -> official name
target_pdx     <- "C0331-231"
example_sgrnas <- c("MYC_2", "ILK_3")      # a third example is chosen below
base_seed      <- 1244                     # same as 16.Rmd
obrien_cutoff  <- -0.1                     # slope below -0.1 = clearly decaying
fig_dir        <- "figures_thesis"
dir.create(fig_dir, showWarnings = FALSE)

## -----------------------------------------------------------------------
## 1. DATA: positive counts of the gene-targeting sgRNAs of C0331-231
## -----------------------------------------------------------------------
raw <- read.csv(data_file, stringsAsFactors = FALSE, check.names = FALSE)
if ("dataset" %in% names(raw)) raw <- raw[trimws(raw$dataset) == target_pdx, ]
raw$M <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(raw$M))
raw <- raw[is.finite(raw$M) & raw$M > 0, ]
raw <- raw[tolower(trimws(raw$gene)) != "ctl", ]   # control guides excluded

map <- read.csv(map_file, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
raw$sgRNA_index    <- as.integer(raw$sgRNA)
raw$sgRNA_official <- trimws(map$name[match(raw$sgRNA_index, as.integer(map$sgRNA))])
if (anyNA(raw$sgRNA_official)) stop("Some sgRNAs have no official name in the map file.")

samples  <- split(raw$M, raw$sgRNA_official)
index_of <- tapply(raw$sgRNA_index, raw$sgRNA_official, function(v) v[1])
cat("Gene-targeting sgRNAs:", length(samples), "\n")

## -----------------------------------------------------------------------
## 2. FUNCTIONS (from tail_index_diagnostics.R)
## -----------------------------------------------------------------------
hill_est <- function(x, k) {
  xs <- sort(abs(x), decreasing = TRUE)
  if (k >= length(xs)) stop("k must be smaller than sample size")
  kappa_hat <- 1 / (mean(log(xs[1:k])) - log(xs[k + 1]))
  se <- kappa_hat / sqrt(k)
  c(kappa_hat = kappa_hat, se = se,
    lower = kappa_hat - 1.96 * se, upper = kappa_hat + 1.96 * se)
}

## Hill estimate for every k from 15 to 35% of the sample (grid of 16.Rmd)
hill_curve <- function(x) {
  k <- 15:floor(0.35 * length(x))
  data.frame(k = k, kappa_hat = sapply(k, function(kk) hill_est(x, kk)["kappa_hat"]))
}

running_moment <- function(x, q) cumsum(abs(x)^q) / seq_along(x)

obrien_slope <- function(x, n_points = 60, n_perm = 40) {
  n <- length(x)
  idx <- unique(round(exp(seq(log(50), log(n), length.out = n_points))))
  logratio_mat <- matrix(NA_real_, n_perm, length(idx))
  for (p in 1:n_perm) {
    xp <- sample(x)                 # random permutation = another valid path
    cs <- cumsum(abs(xp))
    cm <- cummax(abs(xp))
    logratio_mat[p, ] <- log(cm[idx] / cs[idx])
  }
  avg_logratio <- colMeans(logratio_mat)
  fit <- lm(avg_logratio ~ log(idx))
  list(slope = unname(coef(fit)[2]), avg_logratio = avg_logratio, idx = idx)
}

## dAMSE from the tea package (same call as in 16.Rmd)
damse_fit <- function(x) {
  out <- c(alpha = NA_real_, k = NA_real_, threshold = NA_real_)
  if (length(x) < 50 || length(unique(x)) < 5) return(out)
  fit <- tryCatch(suppressWarnings(tea::dAMSE(x)), error = function(e) NULL)
  if (is.null(fit)) return(out)
  c(alpha = as.numeric(fit$tail.index)[1], k = as.numeric(fit$k0)[1],
    threshold = as.numeric(fit$threshold)[1])
}

## -----------------------------------------------------------------------
## 3. DIAGNOSTICS FOR ALL sgRNAs (needed to choose the third example)
## -----------------------------------------------------------------------
diag <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(samples), function(g) {
  x <- samples[[g]]
  d <- damse_fit(x)
  set.seed(base_seed + index_of[[g]])          # same seed as 16.Rmd
  ob <- obrien_slope(x)
  data.frame(sgRNA = g, n = length(x), alpha_damse = d["alpha"],
             k_damse = d["k"], threshold = d["threshold"],
             alpha_lower = d["alpha"] - 1.645 * d["alpha"] / sqrt(d["k"]),
             obrien_slope = ob$slope, row.names = NULL)
}))
diag$obrien_decaying <- diag$obrien_slope < obrien_cutoff

## Third example: dAMSE alpha <= 1 AND O'Brien not decaying (both suggest
## that the mean may not exist); among those, the sgRNA with most observations.
both_negative <- diag[is.finite(diag$alpha_damse) & diag$alpha_damse <= 1 &
                        !diag$obrien_decaying, ]
third <- if (nrow(both_negative)) both_negative$sgRNA[which.max(both_negative$n)] else
  diag$sgRNA[which.min(diag$alpha_damse)]
examples <- c(example_sgrnas, third)
if (any(!examples %in% names(samples))) stop("Example sgRNA not found: ",
  paste(examples[!examples %in% names(samples)], collapse = ", "))

cat("\nExamples used in the figures:\n")
print(diag[match(examples, diag$sgRNA), ], digits = 3)
write.csv(diag, file.path(fig_dir, "ch4_diagnostics_all_sgRNAs.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

colors <- c("#1b9e77", "#d95f02", "#7570b3")
names(colors) <- examples
ex <- diag[match(examples, diag$sgRNA), ]
labels <- sprintf("%s (n = %d, dAMSE alpha = %.2f)", ex$sgRNA, ex$n, ex$alpha_damse)
names(labels) <- examples

## -----------------------------------------------------------------------
## 4. FIGURE 1: EMPIRICAL PARETO-TAIL PLOTS (Section 4.3.2)
## Points: empirical survival P(M > x) on log-log axes.
## Dashed line: Pareto tail with slope -alpha_hat (dAMSE), from the threshold.
## -----------------------------------------------------------------------
surv <- lapply(examples, function(g) {
  x <- samples[[g]]; ux <- sort(unique(x)); s <- 1 - ecdf(x)(ux)
  data.frame(x = ux[s > 0], s = s[s > 0])
})
names(surv) <- examples

pdf(file.path(fig_dir, "ch4_pareto_tail.pdf"), width = 7, height = 5)
plot(NA, log = "xy",
     xlim = range(unlist(lapply(surv, `[[`, "x"))),
     ylim = range(unlist(lapply(surv, `[[`, "s"))),
     xlab = "Clone size x (log scale)", ylab = "Empirical P(M > x) (log scale)",
     main = "Empirical Pareto-tail plots, PDX C0331-231")
for (g in examples) {
  points(surv[[g]]$x, surv[[g]]$s, col = colors[g], pch = 16, cex = 0.6)
  x <- samples[[g]]; u <- ex$threshold[ex$sgRNA == g]; a <- ex$alpha_damse[ex$sgRNA == g]
  su <- mean(x > u)
  if (is.finite(u) && is.finite(a) && su > 0) {
    xs <- exp(seq(log(u), log(max(x)), length.out = 50))
    lines(xs, su * (xs / u)^(-a), col = colors[g], lwd = 2, lty = 2)
  }
}
legend("bottomleft", legend = labels, col = colors, pch = 16, lty = 2, lwd = 2,
       bty = "n", cex = 0.8)
dev.off()

## -----------------------------------------------------------------------
## 5. FIGURE 2: HILL PLOTS (Section 4.4, re-examination)
## Hill estimate as a function of k; the dotted line marks alpha = 1.
## -----------------------------------------------------------------------
hill <- lapply(examples, function(g) hill_curve(samples[[g]]))
names(hill) <- examples

pdf(file.path(fig_dir, "ch4_hill_plot.pdf"), width = 7, height = 5)
plot(NA, log = "x",
     xlim = range(unlist(lapply(hill, `[[`, "k"))),
     ylim = range(c(0.5, unlist(lapply(hill, `[[`, "kappa_hat"))), finite = TRUE),
     xlab = "Number of upper order statistics k (log scale)",
     ylab = expression(hat(alpha)[H](k)),
     main = "Hill plots, PDX C0331-231")
abline(h = 1, lty = 3, col = "grey40")
for (g in examples) lines(hill[[g]]$k, hill[[g]]$kappa_hat, col = colors[g], lwd = 2)
legend("topright", legend = labels, col = colors, lwd = 2, bty = "n", cex = 0.8)
dev.off()

## -----------------------------------------------------------------------
## 6. FIGURE 3: O'BRIEN MAXIMUM-TO-SUM DIAGNOSTIC (Section 4.4)
## Downward-sloping line = mean exists; flat line = mean does not exist.
## -----------------------------------------------------------------------
ob <- lapply(examples, function(g) {
  set.seed(base_seed + index_of[[g]])          # same paths as in 16.Rmd
  obrien_slope(samples[[g]])
})
names(ob) <- examples

pdf(file.path(fig_dir, "ch4_obrien.pdf"), width = 7, height = 5)
xr <- range(unlist(lapply(ob, `[[`, "idx")))
yr <- range(unlist(lapply(ob, `[[`, "avg_logratio")))
plot(NA, xlim = log(xr), ylim = yr, xaxt = "n",
     xlab = "Number of observations n (log scale)",
     ylab = expression(log(M[n] / S[n]) ~ "(permutation-averaged)"),
     main = "O'Brien maximum-to-sum diagnostic, PDX C0331-231")
axis(1, at = pretty(log(xr)), labels = round(exp(pretty(log(xr)))))
for (g in examples) lines(log(ob[[g]]$idx), ob[[g]]$avg_logratio, col = colors[g], lwd = 2)
legend("bottomleft",
       legend = paste0(examples, sprintf("  [slope = %.3f]", sapply(ob, `[[`, "slope"))),
       col = colors, lwd = 2, bty = "n", cex = 0.8)
dev.off()

## -----------------------------------------------------------------------
## 7. FIGURE 4: RUNNING MEANS (Section 4.5)
## Each running mean is divided by its final value: flat near 1 = stabilized
## (mean exists); jumps or drift = sensitive to extreme observations.
## One random order of the observations per sgRNA (reproducible seed).
## -----------------------------------------------------------------------
rm_curves <- lapply(examples, function(g) {
  set.seed(base_seed + 5479 + index_of[[g]])
  r <- running_moment(sample(samples[[g]]), 1)
  r / r[length(r)]
})
names(rm_curves) <- examples

pdf(file.path(fig_dir, "ch4_running_mean.pdf"), width = 7, height = 5)
plot(NA, xlim = c(1, max(lengths(rm_curves))), ylim = range(unlist(rm_curves)),
     xlab = "Number of observations n",
     ylab = expression(hat(m)[1](n) / hat(m)[1](n[max])),
     main = "Running sample means (normalized), PDX C0331-231")
abline(h = 1, lty = 2, col = "grey60")
for (g in examples) lines(seq_along(rm_curves[[g]]), rm_curves[[g]], col = colors[g], lwd = 2)
legend("topright", legend = examples, col = colors, lwd = 2, bty = "o", bg = "white", cex = 0.8)
dev.off()

cat("\nSaved in", fig_dir, ":\n",
    " ch4_pareto_tail.pdf, ch4_hill_plot.pdf, ch4_obrien.pdf, ch4_running_mean.pdf,\n",
    " ch4_diagnostics_all_sgRNAs.csv\n")
```
